title: Final self-check: Git & GitHub Fundamentals
intro: 40 questions from all five units (8 per unit), freshly mixed every attempt. At the end you get a score for each unit and links to revise. This is practice, not the certificate exam.

questions.q: Meet's laptop crashes. Which kind of version control guarantees his teammates still have the full project history?
options: Centralized, if the server is down
questions.explain: In a distributed VCS like Git, every clone holds the complete history.

questions.q: Which file does git config --global user.email write to?
questions.explain: Global settings live in .gitconfig in your home folder; local ones in .git/config.

questions.q: Which of these can host Git repositories? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explain: Git Bash is a terminal for Windows, not a hosting service.

questions.q: On a shared lab PC, how should you set your name so the next student doesn't commit as you?
questions.explain: A local setting applies only to your repository.

questions.q: Your commit failed with 'Author identity unknown'. What is missing?
questions.explain: Set them with git config, then commit again.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.code:
$ mkdir demo && cd demo
$ git init
$ git status -s
options: Nothing: there are no files yet
questions.explain: A new empty repository has nothing to report. The .git folder itself is never listed.

questions.q: You edited menu.txt after running git add menu.txt. You commit now. What gets saved?
options: The version from when you ran git add
questions.explain: git add copies the content at that moment into the staging area. Add again to include later edits.

questions.q: Which command shows the remote URL of your repository?
questions.explain: git remote -v lists remotes and their URLs.

questions.q: git status says 'Your branch is ahead of origin/main by 2 commits'. What should you do to share your work?
questions.explain: Ahead = you have commits GitHub doesn't. Push them.

questions.q: Why does GitHub reject your account password when you push from Git Bash?
options: GitHub requires browser sign-in (Credential Manager), a token or SSH instead
Pushing is only allowed on weekdays
You must use git pull instead
questions.explain: Account passwords stopped working for Git operations in 2021.

questions.q: You're on main and type git branch feature-x. Which branch are you on now?
questions.explain: git branch only creates. Use git switch feature-x (or switch -c) to move.

questions.q: main and feature-cart both have new commits. What does git merge feature-cart (on main) create?
options: A merge commit with two parents
questions.explain: When both sides moved on, Git combines them in a merge commit.

questions.q: You resolved a conflict in timing.txt but committed with the <<<<<<< lines still inside. What does Git do?
options: Commits them as normal text: you must check the file yourself
questions.explain: Git only checks that you ran git add, not what the file contains.

questions.q: Which shows remote branches too?
questions.explain: -a lists local and remote-tracking branches.

questions.q: Why does a team keep main always working?
options: Everyone starts new work from it and demos it
questions.explain: main is the shared, trusted version; features are built on branches and merged when ready.

questions.q: Which command shows what changed in the commit before the current one?
questions.explain: HEAD~1 is the parent of the current commit; git show displays its message and diff.

questions.q: git stash list shows stash@{0} and stash@{1}. Which is the newest?
questions.explain: stash@{0} is always the most recent.

questions.q: You committed with a typo in the message and have NOT pushed. Quickest fix?
questions.explain: --amend replaces the last commit. Only for commits not yet pushed.

questions.q: After this, what does git log --oneline -1 show?
questions.explain: revert adds a new commit that undoes the previous one.

questions.q: Which is the most dangerous for uncommitted work?
questions.explain: --hard overwrites your files; uncommitted changes are lost.

questions.q: Where does a GitHub repository show its README?
options: Below the file list on the Code tab
questions.explain: The README is the repository's front page.

questions.q: Which setting stops anyone pushing directly to main without a reviewed pull request?
questions.explain: Settings → Branches → require a pull request before merging.

questions.q: In a pull request, which tab shows the code changes?
questions.explain: Files changed shows the diff where reviewers comment on lines.

questions.q: Your fork is behind the original repository. Which command brings in the original's new commits (after adding it as upstream)?
questions.explain: Pull from upstream, then push to your fork if you want it updated on GitHub too.

questions.q: Which files help strangers contribute to an open-source project? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explain: README explains the project, CONTRIBUTING the rules, LICENSE what's allowed.
